patch.value: GH-1148: cached drift mismatch can falsely report tracker corruption

GitHub issue #1148 demonstrates that pm health can combine stat-trusted history and item metadata caches into a history_drift_hash_mismatch verdict that strict authoritative rereads disprove, while the diagnostic omits cache invalidation evidence and remediation.

Metadata-mode health preserves the warm-cache fast path when cached hashes agree; A cached hash mismatch is never emitted until the item document and history stream are reread authoritatively; Stale cache evidence is replaced and the final diagnostic reports that a strict confirmation occurred; Cache schema records the runtime history-hash capability and invalidates incompatible envelopes; Regression and performance controls cover false-positive recovery, genuine drift retention, and zero extra rereads on clean cache hits; SDK CLI health validate and temporary-workspace acceptance retain contract parity and exact coverage
pm 2026.8.24 and 2026.8.28 on a clean long-lived pm-brief workspace

Prime history and metadata caches, restore an older stat-compatible cache state through ordinary git/package operations, then run pm health and compare the hash-mismatch verdict with an authoritative cache-free scan.

A cache may accelerate a clean verdict but can never originate a corruption verdict; any cached mismatch is confirmed against authoritative item files and history streams, stale evidence is invalidated, and diagnostics explain the confirmation path.
pm health reports history_drift_hash_mismatch from gitignored cache state on a clean tracker; deleting runtime caches changes the same tree to ok with no drift and no remediation points at the cache.
SDK health, history drift cache, metadata cache, and diagnostics
A false corruption warning can block releases or induce an agent to rewrite correct immutable history.
